A design leadership decision

One system. Three different customer needs.

Discovery needs exploration; financing needs decision clarity; resident services need dependable repeat interactions. One rigid template would fail all three.

I standardised navigation, feedback and system states while preserving specialist patterns for maps, tours and affordability tools.

The trade-off: align teams on shared rules early to avoid duplicated work and inconsistent behaviour later.

03The system

From customer insight to reusable product foundations.

I translated customer insight into connected journeys, shared interaction patterns and an English/Arabic atomic system, working directly with engineering. Visuals are illustrative reconstructions.

Homeownership is a relationship, not a transaction.

Behavioural research surfaced the real friction: not interest, but trust. Maintenance was the most-needed, least-trusted service category. Buyers wanted clearer pricing and transparent communication before, during and after.

  • Qual + quant studies with prospective buyers and existing residents
  • Service-quality benchmarking across the regional category
  • Findings clustered into themes that set the design priorities
Sophia
Simulated synthesis board · notes to themes

One platform strategy. Three product surfaces.

We examined the established regional pattern of multi-service digital platforms, including Careem and Noon, where customers can move between different everyday needs within a connected service experience. This was useful strategic context, not proof that a property super-app would succeed. Customer research supplied the reason to act: people were switching between disconnected services to discover homes, assess affordability, transact and manage life after purchase. We proposed one property-lifecycle ecosystem, with continuity for customers but specialised experiences for each task.

  • Regional super-app patterns as a reference model; fragmented property journeys as the evidence for the product decision
  • End-to-end IA across onboarding, search, financing, scheduling and aftercare
  • Insight reshaped IA from search → buy to discover → finance → manage → community
Search → Buy → Discover → Finance → Manage → Community

Simulated annotated wireframe

A business case for shared design infrastructure.

I advocated for a shared design system to client and consulting leadership because disconnected teams were duplicating effort and accumulating design and technical debt. I led the development of approximately 3,000 atomic components, from foundations to product templates, and partnered directly with engineers on buildable patterns, consistent feedback and error states, and English/Arabic left-to-right and right-to-left experiences.

  • WCAG 2.1 AA, light/dark, dynamic type, scaling
  • Reusable patterns intended to reduce duplicated effort and design-to-development friction

Simulated component library

Every component, mirrored.

Arabic runs 20 to 30% longer than English. Reading direction flips. Directional icons mirror. We built every atom, molecule and organism in both languages from day one, not as a translation pass.

  • RTL parity, dynamic text scaling, cultural icon review
  • Design-to-dev parity via live Storybook, zero drift between Figma and code
